title: Husband Driving Car Safely Catches Newborn Baby Girl With His Free-Hand As Wife Gives Birth In Passenger Seat, Sparking Breathtaking Insights For AI Self-Driving Cars
text:
‘Tis the season for a feel-good news item.
Please find a comfortable and cozy place to relish this heartwarming account.
A worried husband was rushing his pregnant wife to the hospital in their car when all of a sudden the baby seemingly decided it was time to arrive into this world. The woman began to give birth to the newborn girl, doing so while in the passenger seat next to her frantically driving hubby.
Amazingly, the woman maneuvered in her seat to face backward, had her back propped against the dashboard, with her knees pressing against the seat she was just in, and voila gave birth to the eager newborn. As a astonishing double dose of amazing, the husband reached out with one hand (keeping the other hand on the steering wheel) and managed to catch the baby during the birthing process.
And, yes, all of this took place while the car was zipping along on the highway as the pair were stridently trying to reach the hospital for a more conventional birthing process. The husband afterward noted that his wife was quite composed throughout the in-car experience. We might also provide some accolades for the husband in his double-duty role as a frenzied driver and birthing assistant.
The baby girl, named Rebecca by her doting parents, happily is doing quite fine and all is well. There seems little doubt that the harrowing tale of how she was born will become a memorable part of her life. Her parents are apt to recount the saga, over and over again, and Rebecca will be able to share the wild account with those that she meets and regale them with an enchanting and breathtaking story.
Not wanting to spoil the positive and altogether upbeat mood about the adventure, I will simply and quietly make a few quick advisory points if that’s okay with you.
First, one might question the aspect that the husband did not pull over the car and at least come to a safe stop where available to do so. Admittedly, getting to the hospital was a priority. On the other hand, driving a car in the midst of a birthing effort is perhaps not an as high priority as being settled someplace and being able to directly aid his wife. A tradeoff certainly exists between wanting to expeditiously reach medical care, while at the same time ensuring that the apparently imminent birthing effort occurs in as safe a manner as feasible.
Second, we can also quibble about his driving attentiveness during the process, especially the free-handed catching feat. By his own admission to a reporter, he had just one hand on the steering wheel, and likely his eyes were focused on his wife and newborn, rather than on the active roadway ahead. Suppose he had steered into a passing truck, or swerved dangerously out of his lane, or otherwise inadequately controlled the speeding along of his vehicle.
This is assuredly a form of distracted driving that even exceeds those moments of people watching cat videos or combing their tousled hair while mindlessly driving their multi-ton car that is akin to a somewhat unguided missile.
Third, when the wife opted to maneuver in the front passenger seat, she took off her seatbelt (as so reported in the news). Being in a moving car without wearing a seatbelt is ill-advised. She also turned around, facing backward and placing her backside against the dashboard. I won’t linger on this facet, other than to note that if the husband perchance did any semblance of hard braking or other full-force driving actions, things would not have turned out well, frighteningly so. Sadly so.
Nonetheless, some would abundantly argue that the husband made the right choice to keep driving, and the outcome is presumably demonstrative proof of that strategy. The baby was born successfully. The wife is doing fine. No one got hurt. The car didn’t get into a collision. All are perfectly fine.
What more can you ask for in this topsy-turvy world that we live in?
Let’s perhaps agree that it is wonderous there was a joyous result (regardless of whether the approach taken was sound or not).
A cynic might say that this shouldn’t be considered news per se. Here’s why. The cynic would insist that there are plenty of ongoing stories of women giving birth while in moving cars. This seems to happen with a fair amount of regularity.
Sensibly so, since we rely on our cars to get us around town, and the odds are that when it seems time to give birth, any prudent husband and wife would pile into their car and head over to the hospital. It stands to reason.
An alternative obviously would be to call an ambulance or to have somehow headed over to the hospital well in advance of the birthing activity (the timing can be trickier than it seems), or be prepared to give birth at home, etc. Well, let’s set aside this side tangent for now and maintain our devoted focus on the circumstance of getting caught relatively unawares that the birthing is going to arise during the driving journey.
You see, despite the likely belief that the birth won’t engage during the driving trek, there is a calculated chance that nature or other factors might force the issue and the birthing will begin during the driving journey to the hospital. There are outsized tales of taxi drivers that have had this happen with an expectant passenger in their taxi. A woman hails a taxi to get to the hospital and discovers that the emergent newborn won’t wait. The taxi driver hauls along as fast as possible, meanwhile, the woman gives birth while seated in the back row of the cab.
The point by the cynic is that giving airtime to this recent instance is overblown. We apparently should put this gushingly sentimental story into the ho-hum bucket and move along to other more notable and truly hair-raising news reports.
Shall we try to counterargue with such cynicism?
Yes, we must.
One stridently standout basis for this latest instance as being newsworthy was because the husband was driving the vehicle, plus the husband participated in the birthing process (okay, only in a modicum of a fashion, but, hey, a smidgeon of credit seems plausible to share). The husband was trying to support his wife as best he could. During her time of need, he was there. Obviously, she deserves the preponderance of the newsworthiness, but we can also see this as a touching moment of two people working together in a time of dire stress.
In most other similar cases, the driver typically takes no overt part in the birthing activity. For example, if the woman is in the back row of a cab, we wouldn’t expect that the cab driver would be of much aid and the activity would be occurring out of reach.
In any case, we ostensibly and soberly do not want the driver in any such similar occurrence to be dividing their time and attention. Pick one focus of attention and stick with it, seems to be the advisory mantra. Either keep driving, doing so safely and somehow averting being distracted by what is taking place inside the car, or bring the vehicle to a safe stop and render direct aid as much as possible.
You must make a choice.
But you might be exhorting that sometimes you have to make these vexing kinds of Gordian knot decisions. Life is complicated. It is common that we get caught between a rock and a hard place. Choosing between driving the car as a fully dedicated act versus aiding your birthing wife, that’s a tough one to call, some would assert.
Whoa, I have a solution for this dilemma.
Prepare yourself accordingly.
Think about the advent of AI-based self-driving cars.
Note that there isn’t a human driver involved in a true self-driving car. Keep in mind that true self-driving cars are driven via an AI driving system. There isn’t a need for a human driver at the wheel, and nor is there a provision for a human to drive the vehicle. For my extensive and ongoing coverage of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) and especially self-driving cars, see the link here.
Here’s an intriguing question that is worth pondering: What impact if any will there be on those driving journey giving-birth instances once we have a prevalence of AI-based true self-driving cars?
I’d like to first further clarify what is meant when I refer to true self-driving cars.
Understanding The Levels Of Self-Driving Cars
As a clarification, true self-driving cars are ones that the AI drives the car entirely on its own and there isn’t any human assistance during the driving task.
These driverless vehicles are considered Level 4 and Level 5 (see my explanation at this link here), while a car that requires a human driver to co-share the driving effort is usually considered at Level 2 or Level 3. The cars that co-share the driving task are described as being semi-autonomous, and typically contain a variety of automated add-on’s that are referred to as ADAS (Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems).
There is not yet a true self-driving car at Level 5, which we don’t yet even know if this will be possible to achieve, and nor how long it will take to get there.
Meanwhile, the Level 4 efforts are gradually trying to get some traction by undergoing very narrow and selective public roadway trials, though there is controversy over whether this testing should be allowed per se (we are all life-or-death guinea pigs in an experiment taking place on our highways and byways, some contend, see my coverage at this link here).
Since semi-autonomous cars require a human driver, the adoption of those types of cars won’t be markedly different than driving conventional vehicles, so there’s not much new per se to cover about them on this topic (though, as you’ll see in a moment, the points next made are generally applicable).
For semi-autonomous cars, it is important that the public needs to be forewarned about a disturbing aspect that’s been arising lately, namely that despite those human drivers that keep posting videos of themselves falling asleep at the wheel of a Level 2 or Level 3 car, we all need to avoid being misled into believing that the driver can take away their attention from the driving task while driving a semi-autonomous car.
You are the responsible party for the driving actions of the vehicle, regardless of how much automation might be tossed into a Level 2 or Level 3.
Self-Driving Cars And Handling In-Car Miracles
For Level 4 and Level 5 true self-driving vehicles, there won’t be a human driver involved in the driving task.
All occupants will be passengers.
The AI is doing the driving.
One aspect to immediately discuss entails the fact that the AI involved in today’s AI driving systems is not sentient. In other words, the AI is altogether a collective of computer-based programming and algorithms, and most assuredly not able to reason in the same manner that humans can.
Why is this added emphasis about the AI not being sentient?
Because I want to underscore that when discussing the role of the AI driving system, I am not ascribing human qualities to the AI. Please be aware that there is an ongoing and dangerous tendency these days to anthropomorphize AI. In essence, people are assigning human-like sentience to today’s AI, despite the undeniable and inarguable fact that no such AI exists as yet.
With that clarification, you can envision that the AI driving system won’t natively somehow “know” about the facets of driving. Driving and all that it entails will need to be programmed as part of the hardware and software of the self-driving car.
Let’s dive into the myriad of aspects that come to play on this topic.
First, it is important to realize that not all AI self-driving cars are the same. Each automaker and self-driving tech firm is taking its own approach to devising self-driving cars. As such, it is difficult to make sweeping statements about what AI driving systems will do or not do.
Furthermore, whenever stating that an AI driving system doesn’t do some particular thing, this can, later on, be overtaken by developers that in fact program the computer to do that very thing. Step by step, AI driving systems are being gradually improved and extended. An existing limitation today might no longer exist in a future iteration or version of the system.
I trust that provides a sufficient litany of caveats to underlie what I am about to relate.
We can now turn our devoted attention to the matter of giving birth while inside a self-driving car.
A husband and wife get into a self-driving car and tell the AI driving system that they want to be driven to the nearest hospital. The AI starts the autonomous vehicle and drives them to their desired destination.
Along the way, the wife starts to give birth to their baby girl.
What does the husband do?
If the husband was driving the car, which happens in a conventional human-driven car, we earlier discussed at some length the agonizing quandary of having to choose between continuing to drive versus bringing the vehicle to a halt. Recall that this rendered a very tough choice to be made.
In the case of a self-driving car, the AI is doing the driving. Thus, the husband is fully available to assist his wife. We have completely removed the conundrum of which action should win in the confounding matter of selecting the driving task versus aiding his wife.
I’m sure that a few skeptics might offer a sarcastic remark that maybe this is “worse” since the husband can get embroiled in his wife giving birth and make the situation somehow less palatable for all concerned. Sorry, I am not going to entertain that gloomy notion.
What we can say for sure is that by the husband not being at the wheel, we have certainly wholly expunged the risk of his panicky driving actions. The AI driving system is not going to go bonkers as a human driver might do in such a crisis moment condition. No wild swerving, no divided or distracted attention, and so on.
In that sense, we have managed to attain two birds with one stone (though nobody should be tossing stones at any innocent birds). We have freed up the husband to aid his wife, and we have removed the husband from driving the vehicle which could have otherwise led to severe and dangerous outcomes. The husband and wife are able to confer and work together. No worries about the car or the driving of the car.
That being said, we now draw our attention to what the AI driving system might be able to do in this kind of situation.
Either of the passengers could instruct the AI driving system to safely bring the self-driving car to a halt. As such, the AI would usually dutifully do so. Various parameters typically come to play, such as whether this is a command by the passengers that suggests doing this action gradually and with lots of time available, or whether it is an urgency that has to be undertaken ASAP.
Interestingly, this does bring us back to the question about whether to speed along to get to the hospital, or whether it makes more sense to come to a stop. The new twist is that we don’t need to worry about driving per se. Whichever choice is made, the driving is still going to be consistent and steady.
It would be tempting to keep going and let the AI driving system try to get you to the hospital. Meanwhile, the husband and wife are doing what they can within the confines of the moving vehicle.
We ought to note that this is still a danger. No matter how good an AI driving system might be, you cannot overcome the laws of physics. If the AI driving system is suddenly cut off by another car and has to rapidly make a lifesaving maneuver, this is going to materially impact the passengers. I mention this point because some pundits seem to have fallen for an utterly false and misleading myth that AI driving systems will be perfect drivers and we will never have car crashes ever again.
That’s plain nonsense (see my explanation for why, at this link here).
Anyway, there are many more beneficial aspects in this use case that can leverage the advent of self-driving cars.
One aspect is that the interior of self-driving cars is likely going to be completely redesigned in comparison to conventional human-driven cars. In a self-driving car, there is no need for a set of driving controls. This means that you don’t have to have a steering wheel (nor pedals), and neither is there any need for a fixed-in-place driver’s seat.
The interior of self-driving cars will be considered a somewhat open area. Designs suggest that we will be using swivel seats. These seats can turn in whichever direction you wish to look, and possibly can also slide around within the vehicle on skids of a sort, notching into fixed places throughout the interior. There is also an expectation that the seats will be reclinable. We will be able to go for long roadway journeys and take a nap while the AI is doing all the driving.
For the husband and wife that are jammed up into giving birth while in the autonomous vehicle, they at least will have room to do so. Unlike the setting in a conventional car, they will readily be able to position themselves as needed in a self-driving car. This is bound to be safer too since the interior will have various protective built-in measures for being in such out-of-place postures.
To clarify, I am not suggesting that the interior of a self-driving car is suitable for giving birth. Unless somehow a particular self-driving car was designed for that specific activity, the idea of using an everyday self-driving car for a birthing effort is not recommended and certainly not expected. This is merely a last-ditch effort when no other option seems viable.
There is yet more added substance on this matter all told.
The chances are that most self-driving cars will have large LED displays mounted within the interior of the vehicle. This will allow passengers to watch movies while taking a lengthy roadway trek. More importantly, the belief is that people will undertake real-time meetings or perhaps enroll in and partake in online courses while inside a self-driving car. Imagine that when you go to work each day, you can take an online class and make efficient use of your in-the-car time.
How does this relate to the couple giving birth?
Easy-peasy, the same online real-time displays and interactivity could be used to connect with the hospital. Via cameras pointing inward inside the self-driving car, the doctors and nurses at the hospital could see what is taking place. The couple could interact with the medical professionals and be aided while performing the birthing process.
This is demonstrably a step up in comparison to the couple trying on their own to figure out what needs to be done. Furthermore, the hospital staff can be readying for the arrival of the self-driving car and be instantly able to render aid once the couple arrives there.
Let’s add even more benefits to this circumstance.
Some suggest that self-driving cars should be equipped with carefully chosen fundamental medical equipment, being always available inside the autonomous vehicle at all times. This might be for example a defibrillator, a first aid kit, and so on. Those could be kept in the trunk, and there would be an easy means provided to access the trunk while still residing within the self-driving car (no need to get out of the vehicle to then open the trunk).
In theory, the medical supplies could be handy for this special activity of the couple.
We can next shift to focus on the driving aspects of the self-driving car.
As mentioned, the AI driving system won’t get into a panic. That’s nice. But this does raise an intriguing question. Some pundits assert that self-driving cars will never drive in any illegal manner. The AI will be programmed to always obey the speed limit, and always come to a full stop at Stop signs, etc. We seem to eschew the notion that AI would go beyond the permitted rules of the road.
I’m betting that the husband was likely exceeding the speed limit as he drove to the hospital. This would be a natural inclination. It would seem worth the risk of getting a speeding ticket to try and ensure safer delivery of his baby girl.
The speeding effort though is more than just a ticket earning activity. You can also argue that it is a dangerous activity. At faster speeds, you tend to have less overall control of the vehicle. You might take turns too fast and go spinning out. Other nearby cars might get confounded by your speeding and run into you. Those are all the downsides involved in going over the speed limit.
Should the AI driving system be allowed to go over the speed limit in this case?
You might say that yes, of course, it should be allowed to do so. This though does raise roadway driving risks. On top of that, if we let the AI do so in this case, it becomes a potentially slippery slope, some so contend. We will find ourselves inch by inch allowing the AI to do faster and faster driving. Maybe the birthing situation is okay, which leads us to say that when someone is having a heart attack and is inside a self-driving car that speeding is okay in that circumstance too. We keep finding reasons to let the speeding happen.
All of a sudden, we have speeding self-driving cars aplenty.
One viewpoint is that this will be perfectly fine in a world of all self-driving cars. In short, if we had only self-driving cars on our roadways and absolutely no human-driven cars, we could let the AI driving systems coordinate electronically with each other.
Envision that a self-driving car declares an emergency driving circumstance. Via V2V (vehicle-to-vehicle) electronic communication, the AI informs other nearby self-driving cars to get out of the way and let this particular self-driving car speed past them. In addition, via the use of V2I (vehicle-to-infrastructure) electronic communication, the AI coordinates with traffic signals and other roadway infrastructure to provide a smooth and uninterrupted path to the hospital.
That does sound quite wonderous.
The problem is that it also depends upon the notion of having only self-driving cars on our roadways. This is easy to say, but will likely be a hugely contentious issue. Some human drivers angrily emphasize that you will get them from behind the steering wheel the day that you pry their cold dead hands from the wheel.
Only in some dream world or nirvana are we going to (in the near-term) ditch the 250 million conventional-driven cars in the U.S. today and only make use of self-driving cars. It will take many decades to gradually retire the human-driven cars and replace them with self-driving cars. We don’t know how long that will take and nor whether there will ever be complete ditching of human-driven cars.
I’ve dragged you through that portion of the discussion to bring up the idea that we are going to have to grapple with what we want the AI driving systems to be able to do, given that there will be a lot of human-driven cars mixed into the roadways with self-driving cars. What latitude will self-driving cars have in comparison to human-driven cars?
While you are pondering that heavy thought, we can cover a few other easier thinking topics.
One thing that an AI driving system could readily do is make contact with a police car and potentially seek to rendezvous with it. In other words, the self-driving car could seek to obtain a police escort that could then speed along with the self-driving following behind it. This would seem to boost the legality of the self-driving car being a speedster.
Another form of rendezvous could be with an ambulance. The AI driving system might make electronic contact with the nearest ambulance, sending a message that a birthing effort is underway (as so informed by the passengers, and not be some divine way of knowing this). An ambulance being driven by presumably human drivers might coordinate a meet-up with the self-driving car. The couple would either then transfer into the ambulance, or the ambulance medics might get into the self-driving car to aid in the birthing effort.
Believe it or not, I’ve only touched the surface of the ways in which a self-driving car might behoove this situation. I am not going to exhaustively cover all possibilities herein, and trust that you get the gist of the matter.
Conclusion
If you want to contemplate some added twists and turns, here’s a quick puzzling tangent for you.
Suppose that the self-driving car was part of a fleet of self-driving cars and being made available as a so-called robo-taxi.
Up until this point in this discussion, I’ve kind of left silent the ownership aspects of the self-driving car that is driving along with the couple inside of it. Some ardently claim that there will not be any individual ownership allowed of self-driving cars and they will only be available as robo-taxis. I have debunked this notion and assert this is abject nonsensical reasoning (see my elaborated discussion at this link here).
If the self-driving car was perchance a robo-taxi, consider whether this aspect changes any of the nuances about how things would play out when the couple was inside of the autonomous vehicle and in the midst of the birthing process that suddenly got underway. I’ll leave it to you to mull that one over.
Hint: Yes, the dynamics do potentially change a bit.
All in all, we are still a distance in time from the advent of widely available true self-driving cars. For the time being, we are inevitably going to hear about stories of someone driving a car that lends a hand during an in-car birthing effort. Human drivers will still be at the wheel for the foreseeable future.
To wrap up this seasonally heartwarming tale of the baby girl, Rebecca, born inside a moving car, we might turn our attention to the underpinnings of the name Rebecca. It is said that the name Rebecca generally denotes someone with a pioneering spirit, a born leader, achievement-oriented, and highly focused on accomplishing tough or daring tasks.
Perhaps the future will consist of Rebecca growing up to be an avid engineer and tech leader that designs, builds, and implements state-of-the-art AI-based true self-driving cars. In so doing, she will apply her pioneering spirit and devoted energies to bringing the benefits of self-driving cars to our world.
And to think that she got her initial start in a human-driven car.
That’s got to be some kind of miracle and a seasonally uplifting consideration.

title: Digital Diplomacy: AI As A Tool To Strengthen International Relations
text:
According to Britannica, the main reason for having foreign policies and diplomacy is to protect and further a state’s interests that generally revolve around geographic, economic and cultural factors. Although idealistic, the idea of equity in the distribution of international power can also be a major reason behind maintaining international relationships. To make up for its traditional counterpart’s shortcomings, digital diplomacy tries to achieve the same goals using the digital medium.
Unbeknownst to most people, several nations today have national AI strategies in place to use the technology for various developmental purposes. Accordingly, AI is the perfect tool to facilitate digital diplomacy in the current landscape. Here’s how AI plays its part in creating and strengthening digital diplomacy around the world:
Improving National Policymaking Processes
Amidst today's globalization, the internal politics and national policies of a country can have effects on its relations with other countries. For instance, companies looking to establish themselves in a foreign country will have to follow the laws there with regards to regulation compliance, employment and other factors. Additionally, the interest rates and production capacities in any country are governed by such policies and cause ripples in the global supply chain and fiscal markets.
Due to these reasons and many more, the role AI plays in improving policymaking in your country influences international diplomacy either positively or negatively. Considering that, here's how AI can disrupt the internal policymaking process in your country:
a) Identification
The first phase of any policymaking process is the identification of problem areas that need to be worked on. Once governments or local bodies concerned with making binding decisions identify those, they can create policies to resolve the problems.
As we know, the data processing power and pattern recognition abilities of an 'experienced' AI tool are second to none. Such capabilities are invaluable for policymakers during crises like the ongoing pandemic, natural disasters or others. The basis of machine learning is to monitor such events and dig deep through past archives to know about how countries and governments worked their way out of them. Accordingly, the tools provide their recommendations to the public-sector leaders so that they can make the most effective policies.
In hindsight, the identification of a crisis before it strikes—like detecting the spread of a mysterious pneumonia-causing virus through several cases in hospitals—could have been useful to stop the COVID-19 outbreak when it had not reached pandemic proportions.
b) Formulation
Once an area is identified for which the creation of national policies is necessary, the formulation process enters the picture. After a thorough consideration of projected expenses, benefits and, in general, the odds of a policy working, AI speeds up this process by providing insights and predictive analyses.
Formulation is arguably the most vital aspect of policymaking as it involves elements of trial and error. It requires a significant amount of research, and necessitates the need for policymakers to have an in-depth understanding of the financial and cultural issues within their country. Digital databases can be configured to maintain records of such factors, making the task simpler. AI-powered tools can analyze historical big data and other information from the private sector, public sector, social media and other sources before generating insights for policies to be formulated. Rich and advanced countries can use specially-configured AI systems to optimize their trade-related national policies and improve their national balance of payments.
c) Adoption
After formulation comes the adoption of the newly created policies. The role of AI is perhaps the most pronounced during the adoption phase. The data-heavy insights generated by AI-powered systems help lawmakers and regulators with making measured decisions during the policy implementation phase. Such individuals will be able to understand the above-mentioned problem areas more clearly and implement laws accordingly.
d) Implementation
Widespread implementation follows the adoption of the policies. This stage witnesses the policies turning into fully fleshed-out laws. AI streamlines the implementation phase with automation tools and the analysis of feedback regarding the laws from various sources. AI's influence in this phase enables public sector bodies to make subtle changes to the policies wherever required.
e) Evaluation
The tweaks mentioned in the implementation phase belong to evaluation, the final part of policy creation. AI tools are essential to carry out assessments of the policies created. During the assessment, an AI-powered system will scan policy areas that are vulnerable to fraud and other criminal activities. For instance, in the UK, AI systems assess the viability of a carbon tax that regulates emissions while also evaluating its effect on the productivity of businesses. AI can carry out such assessments much better than human analysts as the technology has more efficient ways of processing information for the task.
All in all, AI not only provides the most accurate insights for national policymaking after going through billions of gigabytes of information but also ensures that the laws created are indeed effective in the real world. If the internal policies of a nation are well thought out and all-encompassing, then such countries bring the world closer to the ideal of digital diplomacy. As we can see, AI will play a part in the process if that ideal target is to be achieved.
Making International Trade More Inclusive
At times, international trade can seem like a closed shop, especially for the poor and underdeveloped nations while they watch the big-league players trading goods and money among themselves. The disparity between the wealthiest countries in the world and the most downtrodden ones is too great, and the general flow of international trade widens that gap further as the years go by. International bodies such as the United Nations and others seek to bridge this gap by making international trade more equitable for everyone. As expected, AI will play a big role in achieving that far-fetched goal.
The United Nations has developed an AI tool that can be used by all countries for attaining valuable trade insights. The tool mainly provides processed information and forecasts regarding which countries to negotiate trade deals with for avoiding seasonal risks, which trade tariffs and taxes to lower for growth, amongst other insights. Most importantly, each suggestion lays out its pros and cons, so countries have information that is not only factually accurate but also actionable to achieve returns.
The United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP) uses the tool named Trade Intelligence and Negotiation Advisor (TINA), to assist policymakers with making better trade decisions after they have checked all the finance and other options available to them.
The website of TINA displays information about the countries that are actively using the tool for optimizing their trade prospects. Apart from that, other information and statistics, such as those regarding finance and trade agreements, are also exhibited on the platform for traders.
The tool studies international trade trends and provides suggestions and forecasts to governments about the products that are in high demand. Using such information, countries can pass policies to reduce tariffs and, essentially, cash in on trade opportunities. Countries like Bangladesh use the tool to negotiate free trade agreements with bigger nations such as India and Pakistan.
Basically, this tool and other trade-related AI systems act as an equalizer of sorts for poor countries in global trade. It is highly useful to improve the trade prospects of poor countries such as Haiti, Tajikistan and Yemen by training data researchers and enabling the political leaders to make more sustainable trade laws with a view to forging trade partnerships with other countries.
The system is designed to facilitate paperless trade processes to make them more inclusive for all the countries in the world. As we know, paperless records save a ton of money and will allow small, medium and large-sized businesses to flourish.
Finally, such a system will serve two more purposes. Firstly, it can help governments in underdeveloped countries know the types of businesses that qualify for financial or policy-based help. In the long-term, the UN is working in partnership with countries such as Cambodia and the Philippines to strengthen such aspects.
And secondly, businesses in debt in developing and underdeveloped countries using TINA will attain information that will enable them to qualify for government aid.
Most importantly, such a tool creates a level playing field for all the countries, whether they are wealthy or underdeveloped. The technological infrastructure, or the lack thereof, in such countries should not be a barrier to international trade. Eventually, with the right laws and decision-making aid—coupled with monetary assistance from the UN for trade purposes—such countries will also be able to harbor ambitions of carrying out huge trade operations and creation of employment. Giving all countries an equal opportunity so that they can build international trade relations with other nations must be a key factor of ideal digital diplomacy, or else the concept will be rendered shallow and meaningless for a large part of the world.
International relationships between countries can exist in several forms—military-based, trade-based and others. Each of those relationships can be bolstered with the help of AI’s abilities. The entire point of using AI for digital diplomacy is to reduce the inequality between countries. As we have seen, AI’s capabilities can be put to good use in several ways by countries and developmental bodies like the UN around the world. Once the world figures a way to address the inequality, then everyone can channelize their resources to fight other issues such as climate change and terrorism.

title: 3 Key Things To Know About The Future Of Content Moderation (And Why Each Matters)
text:
While the internet has been around for a few decades now, the requirements of running an online platform are completely different today than they were 30 years ago. In the past, content platforms had to worry only about gathering users. However, as the amount of information online has expanded exponentially, businesses and content platforms must consider how to ensure their content is both accurate and safe.
In a 2019 survey, 49 percent of adults said they had shared information which they later found out was incorrect. Online content platforms today include massive amounts of unverified information, which, when shared in large numbers, can lead to the spread of deadly infections, violent uprisings and the changing of governments, affecting millions of lives.
Another problem is that the popularity of internet influencers has grown with time, and mixed in with those who are selling harmless and fun products, you’ll find influencers who are promoting extremism or violence. Content moderation today must take all of this into account and keep the internet a safe source for accurate information for the long-term.
In the early stages of the internet, moderators of small platforms may have been able to hire a few people to ensure the content users were sharing was both truthful and non-violent. Today, there’s so much information being shared every second, the field of content moderation requires constant innovation to keep up and continue doing its job.
1. A More Proactive Approach
The language of bad actors on the internet is constantly changing. This means it isn’t enough to run a simple algorithm across your platform looking to filter a specific list of words. Instead, content moderators must proactively identify the ever-changing language of the groups promoting hate speech and violence online.
Creating a database of malicious content allows content moderators to be as proactive as possible. This allows content moderators to search for new terms, ideas and symbols being shared by harmful influencers before they become popular. Without this proactive approach, content moderators must wait until a harmful idea or word grows in popularity before it can set filters to filter out the language.
Noam Schwartz, co-founder and CEO of ActiveFence, commented on the difficulty of identifying hate speech and influencers for evil. “An ISIS-produced video might pop up on a leading social platform without any external indication that it has evil content in it,” he said.
“The title of the video could be something totally random, and nothing identifies it as a video from a terrorist organization unless the viewer is aware of the context and understands its meaning, so regular AI isn’t able to catch and filter it. It’s essential to be proactive about finding that content. We continuously scan, collect and analyze millions of sources proactively, and this approach is highly effective for detecting and eliminating harmful content before it starts to be shared around to massive audiences.”
2. Establishing Trust And Authority
Identifying or removing misinformation will be one of the main issues for content platforms to address in the coming years. Online platforms 30 years ago were rarely seen as the ultimate sources of information. At that time, it was still easier to go to a library for research and check the newspaper for an update on current events. Today, the internet is the most common source of information.
Unfortunately, with the majority of content being consumed and shared online, it’s much more difficult to verify the validity of information before it reaches audiences. The future of content moderation includes finding ways to truly filter misinformation and verify facts before they’re shared. This will allow content platforms to establish themselves as trustworthy sources of information.
Sigrid Zeuthen, global marketing manager of content moderation platform, Besedo, believes users are looking for accuracy in an online platform. Zeuthen says, “Building trust is one of the key components that facilitate transactions in an online marketplace.”
As content moderators improve their ability to identify misinformation, content platforms will have the ability claim authority and gain users. The success of any content platform in the future will rely on strong content moderation.
3. The Need For Advanced Image, Video And Audio Recognition
Written content is becoming increasingly a minority on the internet. It’s being replaced by images, videos or audio content. A lot of early content moderation technology was trained to identify harmful words and written language. As the majority of content moves away from that format, the tools for identifying harmful content will require increasingly innovative technology.
Luckily, the field of artificial intelligence is rapidly advancing. Every day, AI tools become better at identification. As the tools become more advanced, content moderation must be early adopters of the most advanced technology. The content moderation industry will rely on artificial intelligence to keep the information on the internet safe and accurate.
Daniela Rus, director of MIT’s Computer Science and AI Lab spoke about the current state of AI technology when she said, “I think that it’s an extraordinary time where we’re seeing so much progression AI and computing. This progress is accelerating the natural language explosion — our enhanced understanding of how to do language understanding and how to do object recognition — is really powering a wide range of applications.”
While the advancement in AI technology can power a wide range of applications, the field of content moderation will depend on its ability to apply those advancements to its products. Any content moderation platforms that are able to stay ahead of the curve in using more advanced AI will be able to keep the internet safe in the future.

title: Bias in AI-driven recruiting subject of tech watchdog group
text:
Artificial intelligence software is increasingly used by human resources departments to screen résumés, conduct video interviews and assess a job seeker’s mental agility.
Now, some of the largest corporations in America are joining an effort to prevent that technology from delivering biased results that could perpetuate or even worsen past discrimination.
The Data & Trust Alliance, announced on Wednesday, has signed up major employers across a variety of industries, including CVS Health, Deloitte, General Motors, Humana, IBM, Mastercard, Meta (Facebook’s parent company), Nike and Walmart.
The corporate group is not a lobbying organization or a think tank. Instead, it has developed an evaluation and scoring system for artificial intelligence software.
The Data & Trust Alliance, tapping corporate and outside experts, has devised a 55-question evaluation, which covers 13 topics, and a scoring system. The goal is to detect and combat algorithmic bias.
“This is not just adopting principles, but actually implementing something concrete,” said Kenneth Chenault, co-chairman of the group and a former chief executive of American Express, which has agreed to adopt the anti-bias tool kit.
The companies are responding to concerns, backed by an ample body of research, that AI programs can inadvertently produce biased results. Data is the fuel of modern AI software, so the data selected and how it is employed to make inferences are crucial.
If the data used to train an algorithm is largely information about white men, the results will most likely be biased against minorities or women. Or if the data used to predict success at a company is based on who has done well at the company in the past, the result may well be an algorithmically reinforced version of past bias.
Seemingly neutral data sets, when combined with others, can produce results that discriminate by race, gender or age. The group’s questionnaire, for example, asks about the use of such “proxy” data including cellphone type, sports affiliations and social club memberships.
Growing efforts to watchdog AI
Governments around the world are moving to adopt rules and regulations. The European Union has proposed a regulatory framework for AI. The White House is working on a “bill of rights” for AI.
In an advisory note to companies on the use of the technology, the Federal Trade Commission warned, “Hold yourself accountable — or be ready for the FTC to do it for you.”
The Data & Trust Alliance seeks to address the potential danger of powerful algorithms being used in workforce decisions early rather than react after widespread harms are apparent, as Silicon Valley did on matters like privacy and amplification of misinformation.
“We’ve got to move past the era of ‘move fast and break things and figure it out later,’” said Chenault, who was on the Facebook board for two years, until 2020.
Corporate America is pushing programs for a more diverse workforce. Chenault, now chairman of the venture capital firm General Catalyst, is one of the most prominent African Americans in business.
Told of the new initiative, Ashley Casovan, executive director of the Responsible AI Institute, a nonprofit organization developing a certification system for AI products, said the focused approach and big-company commitments were encouraging.
“But having the companies do it on their own is problematic,” said Casovan, who advises the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development on AI issues. “We think this ultimately needs to be done by an independent authority.”
The corporate group grew out of conversations among business leaders who were recognizing that their companies, in nearly every industry, were “becoming data and AI companies,” Chenault said. And that meant new opportunities, but also new risks.
The group was brought together by Chenault and Samuel Palmisano, co-chairman of the alliance and former chief executive of IBM, starting in 2020, calling mainly on chief executives at big companies.
They decided to focus on the use of technology to support workforce decisions in hiring, promotion, training and compensation. Senior employees at their companies were assigned to execute the project.
Internal surveys showed that their companies were adopting AI-guided software in human resources, but most of the technology was coming from suppliers. And the corporate users had little understanding of what data the software makers were using in their algorithmic models or how those models worked.
To develop a solution, the corporate group brought in its own people in human resources, data analysis, legal and procurement, but also the software vendors and outside experts. The result is a bias detection, measurement and mitigation system for examining the data practices and design of human resources software.
“Every algorithm has human values embedded in it, and this gives us another lens to look at that,” said Nuala O’Connor, senior vice president for digital citizenship at Walmart. “This is practical and operational.”
The evaluation program has been developed and refined over the past year. The aim was to make it apply not only to major human resources software makers like Workday, Oracle and SAP, but also to the host of smaller companies that have sprung up in the fast-growing field called “work tech.”
Many of the questions in the anti-bias questionnaire focus on data, which is the raw material for AI models.
“The promise of this new era of data and AI is going to be lost if we don’t do this responsibly,” Chenault said.

title: Council Post: What Challenges In Education Can AI Solve Today?
text:
Dmitry Baraishuk is a Partner and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) at Software Development company Belitsoft with 16+ years of EdTech.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming one of the disruptive factors in the educational area. AI in the education market has been forecasted to grow by 45.12% annually and reach $10.38 billion by 2026.
In general, e-learning makes education available anytime and anywhere, which has become crucial in the pandemic and remote work era. Corporations, education tech startups, training companies, universities, schools and students — all parties get a lot of prominent benefits from online learning, like covering larger audiences online. At the same time, AI boosts e-learning to a new level by addressing challenges that are not obvious at first glance.
Challenge: Filling Skill Gaps By Integrating, Upskilling And Reskilling
Studies show that 9 in 10 executives recognize or expect staff skill gaps over the next five years, and less than half of them know how to overcome this challenge. Fifty-six percent of respondents noted that one of the most popular tactics for addressing the skill gaps is upskilling or reskilling across the organization.
However, approximately 70% of HR professionals are not content with how their organizations address their internal mobility purposes.
An AI-driven individual career path builder can help acquire the necessary skills through a learning experience platform (LXP). An employee, when looking for new opportunities, can use the tool for a clear understanding of the open positions within their organization and the required skills for each role. AI algorithms analyze an individual's current skill set, match the skills against the job requirements, emphasize the missing ones and advise the appropriate courses to fill in these skills gaps.
Challenge: Matching The Right Talent To The Right Roles On A Scale
Corporations, training companies and education tech startups are leveraging AI-based tools for workforce skills assessments that help match the right talent to the right roles on a scale.
How does it work? Humans need to describe the skills only once. Then the machine will parse the data by itself. An AI-based algorithm automatically ranks the job-ready skills of every employee, analyzing their profiles and competency matrix.
Thanks to the implementation of AI in learning and development (L&D) and talent management departments, the manager will get a list of candidates with their ranked level of skills. Additionally, the data will be mapped with the competencies the company needs.
Challenge: Ensuring Faster Knowledge Acquisition And Improving Learning Outcomes
Automatic personalized AI-powered learning path building with targeted content recommendations can help every employee or student in a few ways. For instance, after a learner has passed an initial knowledge check or skills assessment, AI builds a personalized learning path that starts from the most ready-to-learn topic.
Additionally, while going through the topic, a trainee is offered a series of questions with hints and detailed explanations in case of incorrect answers. So the learners complete a certain number of topics and pass the determined amount of hours. After that, the AI knowledge checker automatically reassesses learners to show what topics they’ve retained.
The materials with which a trainee has done well will go to the mastered category, and the topics where they have struggled will move back to the learning path to be reviewed again.
Challenge: Measuring The Effectiveness Of Training Programs
An AI-driven learning progress tracking tool is able to check whether employees or students are mastering or missing the needed competencies. That measures the impact of learning and optimizes it accordingly.
How does it work? The software aggregates data about trainees’ performances and their grades from a learning management system (LMS), including overall scores and competencies, missing assignments or past due assignments.
An AI-powered progress tracking tool analyzes the progress of every learner based on their individual activities and performance. Educators and L&D teams see the gathered data in a single dashboard and get intuitive reports. Also, the system flags students at risk or low-performing employees, allowing educators and L&D managers to follow up quickly.
Challenge: Forecasting Future Learning Outcomes And Potential Problems
The AI-powered predictive analytics tool gathers data about past and current activity. Based on the gathered data, the software builds patterns of learning behavior for each learner and projects future proficiency for final assessments. The system automatically generates precise reports and sends them to educational staff, so they can uncover pitfalls in a timely manner. As a result of early interventions, learners' success rates and retention increase.
L&D departments and educators use predictive reports to help their employees or students make proficiency gains earlier in the learning cycle and address knowledge gaps. The AI-based system also might provide alerts to inform mentors of events that may require their intervention or a discussion.
In addition to the listed challenges, AI in education can address other issues, such as increasing user retention and course completion rates in language learning or reallocating the time of L&D, HR and educational leaders to meaningful and strategic tasks by passing routine tasks to AI chatbots.
Conclusion
Nowadays, you can experience a billion competing products, and the lion’s share of them promise much but deliver little. Realizing what solution is working and what is not for you is crucial.
When investing in an AI-powered LMS, it is important to get proper consulting from e-learning experts. That will help you understand how to integrate AI into your current LMS or maybe create an LMS from scratch.
One of the primary steps is to choose the type of e-learning software that will perfectly suit the target audience and the learning goals, such as AI LMS, LXP, learning mobile or web applications.
Implementing AI features converts a traditional admin-centered LMS into a learner-centered LXP. AI in LXP performs as a recommendation engine, replacing a unified curriculum with personalized learning content.
The core idea of e-learning mobile and web applications is making the process available anytime and anywhere through personal devices.
To get early results, test easy-to-apply solutions. Additionally, it might be more cost-effective not just to replace your legacy systems with completely new ones but to think about opportunities to utilize them in new environments.
